articles.title: Development of a pro-angiogenic stem cell-derived vascular cell extracellular matrix-decorated hyaluronic acid hydrogel.
articles.authors: Louise Hosty, Yu-Yin Joanne Chang, Martina Konečná et al.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are debilitating chronic wounds which affect up to a third of diabetic patients. Due to the underlying diabetic pathophysiology, normal wound healing is perturbed. In particular, there is insufficient re-vascularisation of the wound bed, ultimately leading to the development of chronic wounds. Current treatment protocols are insufficient to stimulate re-vascularisation and wound closure, ultimately leading to ~20% of patients with a DFU requiring lower limb amputation. Extracellular matrix (ECM)-derived biomaterials have demonstrated great promise to promote tissue vascularisation and wound repair. In the present study, the overarching goal was to develop a decellularised ECM from human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived vascular cells, and incorporate it into a hyaluronic acid-based hydrogel for wound healing. Vascular differentiation of hiPSCs yielded a heterogenous population containing both CD31 expressing endothelial cells (iEC), and CD31-negative stromal cells (iSC). ECM deposition by iSCs was stimulated by treatment with ascorbic acid and macromolecular crowder carrageenan. Post-decellularisation, the ECM composition was analysed by immunofluorescent and histological staining, indicating the presence of ECM components such as fibronectin, fibrillar collagens, perlecan and glycosaminoglycans, all having implications in angiogenic processes. Decellularised ECM accelerated the capacity of iECs to form tube-like structures when added to cell culture media in 2D. Decoration of hyaluronic acid (HyA)-based hydrogels with this decellularised ECM enhanced metabolic activity and attachment of both HUVECs and human dermal fibroblasts seeded on these hydrogels. Taken together, this ECM-decorated HyA-based hydrogel has the potential to enhance angiogenesis and revascularisation in chronic wound applications such as DFU.

articles.title: Anatomical and molecular characterization of a regionally heterogeneous intramuscular tendon in the mouse masseter muscle.
articles.authors: Sayo Sekiya, Kei Kitamura, Hidetomo Hirouchi et al.
articles.abstract: The mouse masseter muscle comprises distinct superficial and deep layers, but the tendinous tissue located between these layers remains poorly characterized. In this study, we investigated the anatomical, molecular, and ultrastructural characteristics of this tissue. Serial anatomical and histological analyses demonstrated that the intramuscular tendon (IMT), located between the superficial and deep masseter layers, was anatomically distinct from the superficial aponeurosis-external tendon complex. These structures also exhibited different skeletal attachments: the aponeurosis-external tendon complex attached to the maxilla, whereas the IMT attached to the mandible. Spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed different gene-expression patterns between the aponeurosis and IMT, with several extracellular matrix-related transcripts, including Col16a1, Col13a1, Col5a2, Tnn, Postn, and Col22a1, showing relatively higher expression in the IMT. Within the IMT, several transcripts showed preferential distribution toward the bone-side region, where immunofluorescence analysis demonstrated significantly higher POSTN immunoreactivity than in the middle- and lateral-side regions. BGLAP exhibited a similar but statistically nonsignificant pattern, whereas COL22 was predominantly localized along the myotendinous junction. Transmission electron microscopy revealed distinct cellular characteristics between the middle- and lateral-side regions. In the lateral-side region, spindle-shaped cells were observed, some of which were oriented toward the tendon interior. In contrast, the middle-side region contained cells with elongated cytoplasmic processes extending toward neighboring cells, forming apparent intercellular contacts. IMT-like tendinous structures were also observed in the jaw muscles of spiny dogfish, Cynops pyrrhogaster, and Xenopus laevis. Together, these findings demonstrate that the mouse masseter IMT is anatomically distinct from the superficial aponeurosis and exhibits regional molecular and ultrastructural heterogeneity. This characterization of the normal IMT may provide an anatomical and molecular reference for future investigations into masticatory muscle-tendon-aponeurosis hyperplasia (MMTAH).

articles.title: Normative Measures of Colon Length in Children With Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Aged 11-17 Years, Based on MRI.
articles.authors: Charlotte A L Jonker, R R Gorter, M A Benninga et al.
articles.abstract: To better understand (abnormal) colonic anatomy on imaging, data on normal colonic anatomy in the unaffected population are crucial. We assessed colon lengths in children without constipation on MRI. This retrospective study included patients (< 18 years), who underwent MRI-enterography between 2016 and 2020 for suspected inflammatory bowel disease, and did not meet Rome-IV criteria for functional constipation. Patients with colonic inflammation were excluded. Primary outcome was the mean total colon length/BSA (cm/m2) (95% CI; ±2SD), and the secondary outcomes were total colon length (cm), rectosigmoid length/BSA (cm/m2), and rectosigmoid length (cm). Colon segments were independently measured on coronal T2-weighted MRI using 3D multiple-point measurements. Linear regression was used to evaluate associations between total colon length and sex, age, height, weight, body surface area (BSA). Eighty-one patients (median age 15 years; range 11-17; 53% male) were included. The mean total colon length/BSA was 72.9 ± 21.0 cm/m2. Mean total colon length was 115.8 ± 13.8 cm, mean rectosigmoid length/BSA was 24.2 ± 12.3 cm/m2, and mean rectosigmoid length was 38.2 ± 7.9 cm. Additionally, we assessed colonic segments per age group. Colon length significantly correlated with age (p = 0.03), height (p < 0.001), weight (p < 0.001), and BSA (p < 0.001). In a multivariable linear regression analysis, BSA was significantly correlated with total colon length (95% CI 21.4-49.4; p < 0.0001). This study provides data on colon and rectosigmoid lengths in children, aged 11-17 years, without constipation measured on MRI-enterography. This knowledge can be used for the identification of abnormal colonic anatomy in children with therapy-resistant constipation on imaging.

articles.title: Development of a novel sigmoid notch index and its association with dental status in adult human mandibles.
articles.authors: Thayumanasamy Venkateswaran Guru, Sridharan Neelamegan
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The mandible is constantly altered based on function and age, especially in cases of tooth loss. Although the measurements of Ramus have been extensively studied, the quantitative analysis of sigmoid notch morphology and its proportional relationships has not yet been well documented. In this paper, we propose a new measurement called the Sigmoid Notch In​dex (SNI) to evaluate these relationships. METHODS: A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted on 121 adult dry human mandibles of South Indian origin, categorized based on dental status as completely dentulous (CD), partially edentulous (PE), and completely edentulous (CE). Bilateral measurements including sigmoid notch depth, condyle-coronoid interdistance, condyle height, coronoid height, gonial angle, ramus height, and ramus width were measured using digital calipers and a goniometer. Linear mixed effects models were used to assess the influence of dental status and side. RESULTS: Significant variations were noted in multiple mandibular parameters with regard to their dental status, specifically the gonial angle, ramus height, and condylar measurements. However, there was no significant variability in SNI despite variations in individual parameters. CONCLUSIONS: The SNI appears to be an innovative and reproducible morphometric index that demonstrates stability in relation to proportionality of the mandibular ramus.

articles.title: Generating standing posture finite element models of the spine with radiation-free imaging.
articles.authors: Federica Incatasciato, Peter P G Lafranca, Timothy Tin-Yan Lee et al.
articles.abstract: Finite element (FE) modelling is a powerful tool for investigating spinal biomechanics. Subject-specific finite element models of the spine are commonly built from supine data obtained from CT images, with harmful radiation and without soft-tissue structures. However, a more accurate evaluation of vertebrae and intervertebral disc loading requires the analysis of the subject in upright posture. In this study we propose a radiation-free alternative to create subject-specific standing FE models by combining supine MRI with ultrasound-based 3D spinal curvature assessment in standing posture. Subject-specific supine FE models of T3-L5 were created from synthetic CT (AI-generated from MRI) of 8 children. Dedicated spinal ultrasound was used to detect the positions of the vertebral laminae, which were used as input to convert the FE model from supine to standing. RMSE was found within 1 mm for the fitted vertebral levels. Validation against conventional radiographic measurements showed no statistical difference in sagittal alignment between the two imaging modalities in the lumbar and mid-to-lower thoracic parameters. In addition, the distance between the vertebral centroids measured from radiographs and from the upright FE model in sagittal and coronal plane was found to be less than 6 mm for the fitted levels. In conclusion, we demonstrate the feasibility of using completely radiation-free imaging as an alternative to CT and bi-planar X-ray to build subject-specific, upright, detailed FE models.

articles.title: Concurrent electrical and mechanical adaptations of forearm muscles across graded handgrip intensities: Evidence from EMG and myotonometry.
articles.authors: Abdurrahman Tanhan, Merve Tunçdemir, Tülay Çevik Saldıran
articles.abstract: Grip force production depends on coordinated neural activation and intrinsic muscle mechanical properties; however, their concurrent behavior across graded contraction intensities and potential sex-related differences remains insufficiently characterized. This study examined simultaneous changes in surface EMG (sEMG) activity and myotonometry-derived mechanical properties of the flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) and extensor digitorum (ED) muscles during graded handgrip contractions. Twenty healthy adults (10 women, 10 men) performed isometric grips at rest and at 40 %, 60 %, 80 %, and 100 % of maximal voluntary contraction (MVC). Muscle activation was recorded via surface EMG (RMS), while tone, stiffness, and logarithmic decrement (LD, an inverse index of elasticity) were concurrently assessed using MyotonPRO. Contraction intensity effects were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA, and sex-based comparisons were conducted at each force level. sEMG amplitudes increased progressively with contraction intensity (p < 0.001). Muscle tone and stiffness showed parallel intensity-dependent increases (p < 0.001), whereas LD remained relatively stable. Sex-related differences were limited in sEMG but more evident in mechanical parameters, with males demonstrating higher FDS tone and stiffness and lower LD in the ED muscle (p < 0.05). Increasing grip force induces coordinated neuromuscular activation and mechanical stiffening with parameter-specific responses. Combined sEMG-myotonometric assessment provides an integrated framework for sex-sensitive evaluation of muscle function.

articles.title: Effects of speed, load, and surface on tibial bending moment and stress.
articles.authors: Thomas A Wenzel, Eric B Francis, Tyler N Brown
articles.abstract: This study assessed locomotor speed, body-borne load, and surface on tibial stress and bending. Fourteen recreational runners had tibial bending moments quantified during a jog (3.0 m/s) and run (4.5 m/s) over a flat and uneven surface with and without 15 kg body-borne load. Peak and mean values of AP, ML and resultant tibial stress and bending moments were quantified and submitted to 3-way repeated-measures ANOVA, while stress and bending waveforms were submitted to statistical parametric mapping 3-way ANOVA. During the run, mean and peak AP and resultant tibial bending moments and stress increased (all: p ≤ 0.009), while all stress and bending waveforms were larger from 0 to 11% and 70 to 100% of stance (all: p ≤ 0.031). With the 15 kg load, mean and peak AP and resultant tibial bending moments and stresses increased (all: p ≤ 0.008) and greater waveform from 13 to 36% and 95 to 100% of stance was exhibited for all bending moment and stresses (all: p ≤ 0.043). On the uneven surface, participants decreased mean and peak AP and resultant tibial bending moments and stresses (all: p ≤ 0.010) and used smaller tibial stress and bending waveforms between 0 to 13%, 18 to 20%, and 69 to 86% of stance for all moments and stresses (all: p ≤ 0.033). Faster run speed and heavier load may elevate risk of tibial stress fracture, while traversing an irregular, uneven surface led to significant reduction in tibial stress and may not similarly elevate injury risk.

articles.title: The Applied Sport Science of Professional Male Basketball: A Narrative Review of Current and Emerging Practices.
articles.authors: Matthew Morrison, Jonathon Weakley, Scott McLean et al.
articles.abstract: Basketball is a physically demanding intermittent team sport which requires a multifaceted approach to optimise player preparation, performance, health, and recovery. Quantifying the training and match demands of professional basketball players can help practitioners develop effective strategies for managing fatigue, monitoring training loads, and guiding physical preparation. Sleep and travel disruptions present additional challenges to practitioners and can have deleterious effects on recovery and readiness to compete. Nutrition is also an essential component supporting performance and recovery and should be individualised to the needs of each player. The inherent complexity of basketball requires practitioners to develop a holistic view that considers the interaction between tactical, technical, psychological, and physical basketball-related factors along with external factors from the greater basketball system (e.g., players, coaches, support staff, organisations, schedules, referees, and governing bodies) that can influence performance. Advances in technology continue to shape performance monitoring, injury-risk forecasting, and training methodologies, yet practitioners must be aware of potential risks such as player privacy concerns and the misuse of data. A comprehensive understanding of these factors provides valuable insights for practitioners to develop effective evidence-based strategies and frameworks for working with professional male basketball players.

articles.title: Acknowledgement to Referees and the Editorial Board.
Ethical, methodological, and translational framework for animal studies in physical exercise research.
articles.authors: Ricardo A Pinho, Larissa C Marques, Lei Zhou et al.
articles.abstract: Experimental research involving physical exercise (PE) in animal models has contributed significantly to advancing knowledge in several areas, including physiology, biochemistry, and translational medicine. Despite the widespread use of these models, important concerns remain regarding methodological heterogeneity, limited experimental standardization, reproducibility of findings, and the translational validity of preclinical outcomes. In this context, the present article proposes an integrated decision-making framework for animal-based PE research. The framework complements existing guidelines linking ethical justification, animal welfare, experimental design, exercise prescription, and translational interpretation throughout the different stages of study development. The manuscript is based on international guidelines for animal experimentation, including ARRIVE 2.0, PREPARE, the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, AVMA recommendations, the APS Resource Book for the Design of Animal Exercise Protocols, and recent methodological recommendations for preclinical exercise research in metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. The topics address aspects related to ethical decision-making in the use of animal models, the principles of the 3Rs, selection of species, strain, sex, and age, sample size calculation, inclusion and exclusion criteria, translational validity, and the definition of exercise protocols, including intensity, frequency, duration, equipment, and experimental monitoring. This framework is intended to support more consistent experimental decisions, including selection, justification, and implementation, according to the research question, animal model, and intended translational inference.

articles.title: Influences of sex and time interval on reliability of neuromuscular and motor performance measurements in isometric plantar flexor exercise.
articles.authors: Cayque Brietzke, Júlio Cesar Cesario, Giovanna Marcucci et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Reliable assessment of neuromuscular function is fundamental for interpreting physiological adaptations, yet sex-related influences in the reliability of these assessments remain poorly characterized across different temporal designs. We determined the within-session and between-days reliability of neuromuscular measurements in physically active men and women across multiple time intervals. METHODS: Thirty healthy participants (15♀ and 15 ♂) completed six sessions to assess the reliability of motor output such as maximal voluntary contraction and time-to-task failure during isometric plantar flexion, as well as electrically evoked responses such as H-reflex, M-wave and V-wave. Relative and absolute reliability were calculated in pooled and sex-separated data. RESULTS: Maximal voluntary contraction showed excellent within-session reliability in all groups. This outcome was consistently good in pooled data and in men for between-days sessions, yet only moderate in women. Although acceptable, within-session and between-days reliability of time-to-task failure were more variable in pooled and sex-separated data. Reliability of H-reflex, M-wave and V-wave ranged from good to excellent in within-session data for both sexes. However, between-days reliability was more variable, as men showed a higher reliability in H-reflex whereas women showed a higher reliability in M-wave and V-wave. Apparently, reliability of electrically evoked reflexes was influenced by the interval between measurements in women. CONCLUSION: Maximal voluntary contraction is a reliable outcome to reflect adaptations in plantar flexion-derived motor output regardless of sex and temporal designs. Results suggested that sex-related influences affect the reliability of electrically evoked reflexes, challenging their ability to reflect biological adaptation of neuromuscular function.

articles.title: Decoupling the neurovascular axis: autonomic and hemodynamic determinants of intracranial pulse wave morphology via principal component analysis.
articles.authors: Alinne Alves Oliveira, Joanderson Felipe Soares Silva, Diego Rocha Cardoso et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study investigated the integrated relationship between systemic hemodynamics, autonomic modulation, and non-invasive intracranial pulse wave morphology (P2/P1 ratio) across na adult age range under basal seated resting conditions. METHODS: Two hundred ninety-nine healthy volunteers (137 males, 162 females; mean age 48.74 ± 24 years) were evaluated. Blood pressure, heart rate, symbolic heart rate variability (0 V, sympathetic; 2UV, parasympathetic), and P2/P1 ratio via scalp extensometry were recorded. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with Varimax rotation was applied to eight normalized variables (Age, HR, SBP, DBP, PP, 0 V, 2UV, and P2/P1). RESULTS: Four components explained 85.81% of variance. PC1 (34.04%) comprised age (loading 0.802), PP (0.824), SBP (0.883), and P2/P1 (0.647), representing an age-pulsatile axis. PC2 (25.46%) captured autonomic dynamics, dominated by 0 V and 2UV. PC3 (13.93%) was dominated by DBP, whereas PC4 (12.38%) showed a P2/P1 loading (0.560). Spearman analysis showed associations of age with P2/P1 (ρ = 0.623, p < 0.05), PP (ρ = 0.479, p < 0.05), and SBP (ρ = 0.472, p < 0.05). P2 > P1 morphology was more frequent among older participants and higher PP. CONCLUSION: Under basal seated resting conditions, P2/P1 was associated with age and pulsatile hemodynamics, particularly PP, while autonomic modulation represented a partially distinct component. The P2/P1 variance in PC4 suggests additional factors not captured by the systemic variables examined. These findings support this non-invasive framework as an exploratory approach for studying cerebrovascular and craniospinal dynamics across adulthood, but do not establish causality or equivalence with invasive measurements.

articles.title: Leg glucose uptake and substrate utilisation during time trial exercise: Effects of acute hypobaric hypoxia and biological sex.
articles.authors: Anders Aagaard Hansen, Marcos Martin-Rincon, Bjarne Rud et al.
articles.abstract: Hypoxia reduces exercise performance, yet it remains unclear how biological sex and altitude influence substrate utilisation during prolonged maximal exercise. Twenty-two trained cyclists and triathletes (10 females) completed 30 min time trials (TTs) at low altitude (normoxia; ∼400 m) and moderate altitude (hypoxia; ∼2800 m in a hypobaric chamber) in counterbalanced order. Whole-body metabolism was estimated from indirect calorimetry, whereas leg glucose uptake and substrate utilisation were derived from arterial and femoral venous blood samples and leg blood flow (thermodilution). Muscle biopsies were obtained from vastus lateralis to measure glycogen utilisation. Across altitudes, females displayed a higher fractional utilisation of V ̇ O 2 max during the TTs. TT performance was decreased in hypoxia, and the proportional decrease was smaller in females (-14%) than in males (-18%). Whole-body substrate utilisation was similar between sexes in normoxia. However, males showed a large decrease in carbohydrate oxidation in hypoxia, whereas females displayed only a modest decrease. Males and females had similar leg metabolic responses to hypoxia: estimated glycogen oxidation decreased, with no change in absolute fat or blood glucose oxidation. However, across altitudes, females showed greater carbohydrate contributions, originating primarily from blood glucose rather than muscle glycogen. Estimates of fat contribution were uncertain but suggested a lower contribution in females than in males. In conclusion, females exercised at a higher relative intensity and derived relatively more energy from blood glucose. Males and females had similar leg metabolic responses to hypoxia, with the lower power output and metabolic rate in hypoxic TTs primarily regulated by reduced estimated glycogen oxidation. KEY POINTS: Substrate utilisation during exercise is affected by altitude, sex, training status, food intake and relative intensity. Whether sex- and altitude-related differences in substrate utilisation persist during an ecologically valid maximal time trial in the fed state in trained males and females is unknown. Acute hypobaric hypoxia (∼2800 m) decreased 30 min time trial performance compared to normoxia (∼400 m) in both sexes, with a larger decrement in males. Females completed the time trials at a higher relative intensity than males in normoxia and hypoxia. Hypoxia reduced total metabolic rate primarily by decreasing estimated muscle glycogen oxidation, with no change in fat or blood glucose oxidation. The resulting changes in substrate partitioning were similar between sexes. Across altitudes, females derived relatively more energy from blood glucose despite similar muscle glycogen utilisation between sexes, whereas uncertain estimates suggested a lower contribution of fat in females than in males.

articles.title: Targeting pepsin provides superior protection to acid suppression in reflux-associated airway inflammation and lung dysfunction.
articles.authors: Thiago Meneses Araújo Leite Sales, Humberto Barbosa da Costa Filho, Kalinne Kelly Lima Gadelha et al.
articles.abstract: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease is a prevalent condition associated with extra-oesophageal manifestations, such as pulmonary inflammation. Pepsin, an essential gastric enzyme, has been implicated in pulmonary complications owing to its inflammatory effects. Although acid-suppressive therapies, such as proton pump inhibitors, reduce gastric acidity, they do not prevent reflux episodes, microaspiration or the harmful effects of pepsin. This study evaluated the effects of pepsin inhibition by pepstatin on inflammation and pulmonary dysfunction in a murine model of reflux. Male Swiss mice were anaesthetized with ketamine and xylazine and subjected to a surgical procedure involving pyloric stenosis and complete stenosis of the gastric fundus to induce reflux. The mice were divided into four groups: sham, reflux, reflux + pepstatin and reflux + omeprazole. Treatments were administered daily for 28 days. The evaluated parameters included oesophageal and pulmonary wet weights, myeloperoxidase activity, cytokine levels [interleukin (IL)-6, IL-10 and keratinocyte chemoattractant], histopathological alveolitis scores, functional analyses of spirometry and tracheal contractility. The reflux group exhibited significant oesophageal and pulmonary oedema, increased myeloperoxidase activity, elevated levels of IL-6 and keratinocyte chemoattractant, reduced IL-10, severe alveolitis, impaired pulmonary function and tracheal hyper-reactivity. Pepstatin treatment significantly reduced inflammatory and functional alterations in the reflux model. In contrast, omeprazole was less effective at controlling inflammation and improving pulmonary function. These findings suggest that pepsin inhibition might reduce pulmonary inflammation and help to preserve lung function in a murine reflux model. Targeting pepsin, rather than solely suppressing gastric acidity, shows promise in mitigating reflux-related extra-oesophageal complications.

articles.title: Intermittent Normobaric Hypoxia and Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Adults: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Pedro Navarro-Gómez, Josep Vidal-Conti
articles.abstract: Intermittent normobaric hypoxia is used as a hypoxic-conditioning strategy in sport, exercise, and health settings, but its effects on cardiac autonomic modulation remain unclear. This review synthesised passive and exercise-combined protocols in adults. We searched 4 databases through March 2026 and reported the review according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I; findings were synthesised narratively, and certainty was graded for coherent evidence. Of 4,866 records, 18 studies were included, 12 arising from controlled parent designs. Controlled resting evidence for the root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) comprised 3 comparisons involving 47 analysed participants. Of these, 2 multiweek comparisons (n = 34) showed numerically concordant between-group differences in RMSSD change, whereas 1 single-session crossover comparison (n = 13) did not establish a clear between-condition effect; certainty was very low in both strata. Frequency-domain heart rate variability evidence was sparse and methodologically unstable, baroreflex sensitivity findings were non-convergent, and exercise-combined evidence was insufficient for directional inference. Heterogeneous dosing, limited sham control, and limited respiratory monitoring restricted interpretation. Evidence remains insufficient to establish reproducible cardiac autonomic changes after intermittent normobaric hypoxia. Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261338890.

articles.title: LACTATION AND FOOD SUPPORT DELIVERY THROUGH THE CANADA PRENATAL NUTRITION PROGRAM IN ONTARIO: A QUALITATIVE STUDY.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Alison Mildon, Jo-Anna B Baxter, Bronwyn Underhill et al.
articles.abstract: The Canada Prenatal Nutrition Program (CPNP), funded federally since 1995, aims to improve birth outcomes and breastfeeding among families facing health inequities through tailored, community-based delivery of perinatal health and nutrition services. To explore Ontario CPNP coordinators' perspectives and experiences delivering lactation and food supports, including changes over time, this qualitative study engaged coordinators working at multiple Ontario CPNP sites. A total of 28 individuals participated from 26 CPNP sites, 15 hosted by community agencies, 6 by Indigenous-led agencies and 5 by public health units. Focus group discussions were conducted at five locations across Ontario, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Three interpretive themes were generated. The first, overarching theme is that the CPNP delivery model is highly precarious due to limited, static funding, resulting in heavy reliance on external and in-kind resources; this affects all aspects of program delivery, including lactation and food supports. Second, accessible, tailored lactation support includes much more than education, and the CPNP is well-positioned to deliver this with adequate human and financial resourcing. Third, food supports are essential to the CPNP, contributing to both nutrition and social aspects of programming. Overall, lactation and food support delivery within the CPNP is responsive to client needs and the broader context of social determinants of health, but constrained by available resources. This study centres perspectives of community-based implementers of the CPNP, offering insights to inform planning, resourcing and programmatic guidance for community programs seeking to reduce health inequities during the critical perinatal period.

articles.title: Protein restriction amplifies nucleus accumbens dopamine responses to protein-rich food during operant feeding in male mice.
articles.authors: Hamid Taghipourbibalan, Stefan W Huijgens, K Linnea Volcko et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Animals strongly defend protein intake, but how protein status shapes moment-to-moment reward signalling in mesolimbic circuits remains unclear, particularly when the effort required to obtain food varies. OBJECTIVE: We tested whether dietary protein restriction altered nucleus accumbens (NAc) core dopamine signalling when mice worked for food of differing nutritional value in the home cage. METHODS: Under surgical anaesthesia, male C57BL/6 mice (n=12; ∼12 weeks old at diet initiation) were injected in the NAc core with a virus expressing the fluorescent dopamine sensor GRABDA and implanted with fibre-optic cannulas. In food-access tasks, nose pokes delivered either chow (protein-containing) or sucrose pellets. Across sessions, pellets required either one nose poke (FixedRatio1) or an increasing number (ProgRatio). Fibre photometry measured dopamine release for both pellet types and schedules during three dietary phases: non-restricted diet (NR1; 18% protein), protein-restricted diet (PR; 4%), and restored non-restricted diet (NR2), with 1 week of adaptation between phases. Behavioural and photometry data were analysed using repeated-measures ANOVA. RESULTS: Home-cage food intake remained stable, but bodyweight gain fell markedly during PR and partially recovered in NR2 (+10.1% NR1 vs. +1.2% PR vs. +6.0% NR2, p<.001). Nose poking increased during PR under both schedules, most robustly for chow pellets (188% and 261% increases under FixedRatio1 and ProgRatio, respectively; ps<.01). Neural effects were more selective. During FixedRatio1, pellet delivery evoked a larger NAc dopamine response to chow than sucrose specifically during PR (p=.001); no pellet-type difference occurred during NR1 or NR2 (ps>.05). During ProgRatio, dopamine responses at pellet delivery and retrieval did not differ between pellet types in any phase (all ps>.05). CONCLUSIONS: Protein restriction did not globally amplify reward-related behaviour or dopamine signalling. Instead, it selectively biased NAc dopamine according to the animal's nutritional status, nutrient context, and task demands.

articles.title: The effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition and influence of FTO genotype in exercise-trained men and women.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.authors: Siavash Naddafha, Antonio Cristani, Kendall Andries et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: High-protein diets have consistently been associated with favorable changes in body composition in both sedentary and exercise-trained populations. Despite abundant evidence supporting protein intakes above the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for active individuals, the effects of deliberate protein overfeeding, particularly in those already consuming adequate protein, remain incompletely characterized. The primary purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition in exercise-trained men and women. The secondary purpose was to determine whether body composition adaptations differed by FTO rs9939609 genotype. METHODS: Fifty-six exercise-trained men and women (age: 22.40 ± 5.78 years; body mass: 75.47 ± 14.98 kg; BMI: 24.52 ± 3.50 kg/m2; resistance training: 5.12 ± 3.35 h/week) were enrolled in a 4-week dietary intervention. Participants were instructed to increase their daily protein intake by approximately 20% above baseline while maintaining habitual training. Body composition was assessed pre- and post-intervention using a multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance device (InBody® 270). Dietary intake was self-monitored via MyFitnessPal®. Thirty-five participants completed both pre- and post-testing assessments and constituted the primary analysis. Linear regression models adjusted for baseline values indicated that FTO genotype was not a significant predictor of body composition changes (p > 0.05). RESULTS: Protein intake trended toward a significant increase over the 4-week period (pre: 146 ± 66 g/day vs. post: 164 ± 79 g/day; p = 0.053), representing an approximate 12% increase. Total energy intake, carbohydrate, and fat intake did not significantly change. Lean body mass increased significantly (pre: 59.95 ± 14.14 kg vs. post: 60.62 ± 14.42 kg; p = 0.005; Cohen's d = 0.31) and total body water increased significantly (pre: 43.85 ± 10.35 L vs. post: 44.34 ± 10.55 L; p = 0.005). Fat mass (p = 0.424), body fat percentage (p = 0.149), and total body mass (p = 0.09) did not significantly change. CONCLUSIONS: A 4-week modest protein overfeeding protocol in exercise-trained men and women was associated with a significant increase in lean body mass and total body water without concomitant increases in fat mass. These adaptations were not modified by FTO rs9939609 genotype. These findings support the contention that higher protein intakes do not promote fat accretion and may facilitate improvements in body composition in trained individuals.

articles.title: From compartments to dynamic physiology: toward actionable body composition.
articles.authors: Karl E Friedl, Adam W Potter, Jennifer L Miles-Chan et al.
articles.abstract: The 12th International Symposium on In Vivo Body Composition Studies (ISBCR 2025) highlighted a fundamental transition from estimating static tissue compartments to dynamic physiological phenotyping, actionable interpretation, and demonstrable value for clinical decision-making, health prediction, and human performance assessment. This represents an evolution in technological capability and conceptual framing, as an extension of the Functional Body Composition concept. Classical multicompartment models and established methods such as dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, isotope dilution, bioimpedance, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging remain foundational; however, emerging approaches increasingly integrate advanced imaging, artificial intelligence, bioimpedance spectroscopy, stable isotope methods, wearable sensing, and multidimensional phenotyping. Several themes were prominent at ISBCR 2025, including expansion of imaging beyond traditional DXA paradigms, increasing emphasis on muscle quality and fluid compartments, greater attention to visceral and ectopic adipose tissue, clinical applications in oncology and critical illness, the evaluation of obesity pharmacotherapy, the importance of generalizability to individuals across sex and ethnicity, and data governance. This perspective proposes a framework for future research in which body composition measurements become integral components of predictive models of health, performance, and physiological resilience. Future body composition assessment practices must include demonstrated added value over previous methods, and the greatest advances will come from technologies that bring physiologically meaningful assessment to large populations. The success of future technologies should be judged less by how precisely they estimate tissue compartments than by how effectively they improve physiological understanding, prediction, and decision-making.

articles.title: Overcoming geographical and cultural bias in dietary assessment: a local food database and photograph-assisted 24-h recalls improve accuracy in Colombian adults.
articles.authors: Vanessa Corrales-Agudelo, Olga Lucía Ortega-Sierra, Mariana Hernández et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate dietary assessment in non-Western populations is hindered not only by recall bias but also by the limited representation of local foods in international reference databases. When standardised tools fail to capture regional dietary practices, the quality of dietary assessments is potentially compromised. This cross-sectional study evaluated the accuracy of photograph-assisted 24-h recalls (24hr) analysed using the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Automated Self-Administered 24-Hour Dietary Assessment Tool (ASA24) system (based on Food and Nutrient Database for Dietary Studies (FNDDS) 2017-2018) or a customised database enriched with local foods and international measurement units (DbF). Twenty Colombian adults photographed and weighed foods consumed over two non-consecutive days. A dietitian conducted 24hr interviews using the multiple-pass method based on the photographs. Intake estimated with ASA24 and DbF was compared against weighed food records as reference. Blood and urine samples were collected to assess nutrient biomarkers. Accuracy was evaluated using correlation analyses and Bland-Altman plots, while usual intake was estimated using PC-SIDE. Misreporting was similar between ASA24 and DbF (15 %). However, DbF improved accuracy, showing stronger correlations with weighed foods for calories and macronutrients (ρ > 0·90) and narrower limits of agreement for energy intake compared with ASA24 (-364 to 256 v. -771 to 909 calories, respectively). DbF allowed estimation of twenty-eight nutrients compared with twenty using ASA24 and showed stronger correlations for micronutrient intake estimates (r 0·86-0·96 v. 0·69-0·96; all P < 0·05) and urinary biomarkers (r > 0·6, P < 0·0001). These findings demonstrate that integrating locally contextualised food databases with technology-assisted recalls improves the quality of dietary assessment in underrepresented populations and provides a scalable model to enhance nutritional epidemiology and health monitoring worldwide.

articles.title: Studying multiple health behaviours in older adults using a measurement burst design: protocol, feasibility, compliance, behavioural patterns and lessons learned.
articles.authors: Kim Cnudde, Laura Maenhout, Femke De Backere et al.
articles.abstract: Overweight and obesity are major public health challenges, requiring preventive efforts targeting diet, physical activity (PA), sedentary behaviour (SB) and sleep. Current research often treats these behaviours in isolation, ignores daily fluctuations and focuses on between-person differences. Studies examining the temporal covariance of these behaviours, assessing within-day and day-to-day variations in determinants and exploring how these time-varying determinants predict within-person variability in behaviours are needed. This paper aims to evaluate the feasibility of a measurement burst design with repeated intensive longitudinal assessments and to present patterns of behaviours and determinants. A 12-month observational study with a measurement burst design was conducted (January-December 2025). In total, 130 participants aged 55-75 years enrolled in the study, which consisted of four 7-day measurement bursts. Data collection included monitoring of diet, PA, SB, sleep and time-based ecological momentary assessment (EMA). Compliance rates, descriptive statistics per burst and across bursts were computed. 116 participants completed all bursts (retention rate = 89·2 %). Compliance rates ranged from 83·5 % for time-based EMA to 91·8 % for SB, supporting feasibility of the protocol. Mean values of 1692 kcal/day (sd = 565) for energy intake, 9·4 h/day (sd = 2·4) for sedentary time and 10 610 steps/day (sd = 6302) were observed. Mean daily light, moderate and vigorous PA-levels were 102·9 (sd = 37·4), 65·5 (sd = 43·4) and 11·5 (sd = 17·0) minutes, respectively. Mean sleep duration was 6·4 h/night (sd = 1·3), with a mean sleep efficiency of 79·2 % (sd = 10·2). This paper demonstrated the feasibility of integrating multiple assessment methods within a measurement burst design for studying health behaviours in adults aged 55-75 years and highlighted the value of analyses at more fine-grained temporal and individual levels.

articles.title: Perceptions and Attitudes Toward Plant-Based Meat Alternatives: A Systematic Meta-Ethnography Review.
articles.authors: Lucrezia Caselli, Clara Gómez-Donoso, Carmen Vargas et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Plant-based meat alternatives (PBMAs) can support the transition toward healthier and more sustainable dietary patterns. However, PBMA adoption remains limited despite availability and awareness of health and environmental benefits, highlighting a gap between potential and practice. OBJECTIVE: This review sought to synthesize evidence on perceptions and attitudes toward PBMAs across populations and to examine how sociodemographic factors shape consumer perspectives. DATA SOURCES: A comprehensive search was conducted across MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Greenfile, and Cochrane from inception to August 2025. DATA EXTRACTION: This systematic review was informed by meta-ethnographic principles (4 to 6), while qualitative data were synthesized using thematic synthesis. Qualitative data from eligible studies were analyzed using a thematic synthesis assisted by ATLAS.ti software and an inductive and iterative approach for coding. Quality assessment employed the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) checklist, and confidence in findings was evaluated using the GRADE-CERQual (Confidence in Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research) approach. DATA ANALYSIS: This review included 31 studies with a total of 2425 participants (aged 9 to > 65 years) from the Asia-Pacific (n = 14), Europe (n = 14), the United States (n = 1), and the United Kingdom (n = 4). Analysis of 914 quotations identified 6 themes (12 subthemes): with moderate GRADE-CERQual confidence, including dietary options, food ethics, dietary perceptions, food openness, food preferences, and dietary drivers; high confidence for dietary alternatives and substitutes; and low confidence for animal ethics. Younger participants (aged <18 years) linked PBMAs with identity and experimentation, while middle-aged adults showed both critical evaluation and resistance. Women demonstrated greater awareness and culinary engagement; men expressed stronger reluctance tied to masculinity. High-income countries exhibited culinary narratives linked to sociocultural values, whereas low- and middle-income countries emphasized affordability and access barriers. CONCLUSIONS: Acceptance of PBMAs is shaped by intersecting sociodemographic factors that reflect broader social identities, moral values, and structural inequities. Future research should adopt intersectional and gender-informed approaches while prioritizing underrepresented low- and middle-income country contexts. PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251114306.
